Title[3076089]: Developmental Dilemmas: The Role of Power and Agency
Description[3076095]: A scholarly monograph examining why developmental policies often fail, focusing on the roles of power, agency, and collective-action problems in economic and political development. The book develops a conceptual framework to analyze how powerful agents shape institutional evolution and developmental trajectories through mechanisms of power, leadership, brokerage, and institutional entrepreneurship. Drawing on case studies and theoretical models, it addresses collective-action problems, resource conflict, social identity, and institutional change, with particular attention to the interplay of formal and informal institutions in shaping outcomes. The work is intended for advanced students, researchers, and policy analysts in development economics and political economy.
